definitions.name: tables_list_tables
definitions.description: Lists the tables of the Nextcloud Tables app the authenticated user can open: their own, the ones shared with them and the ones of the applications (contexts) they belong to. Each table has an id, its title, whether the user owns it and a link; viewsListed says whether tables_list_views lists its views (only for tables the user owns or manages, as in the Tables app). Read only; it creates nothing. Use limit and offset for more.

limit.description: Maximum number of tables returned (default 50, at most 200).

offset.description: Number of tables to skip, from nextOffset of the previous page (default 0).

definitions.name: tables_list_views
definitions.description: Lists the views of the Tables app the authenticated user can open: the views of the tables they own or manage, the views shared with them and the views of their applications (contexts). A view shows only some rows and columns of its table. Views of a table shared without manage permission are not listed, as in the Tables app; the table itself is. Read only. Use limit and offset for more.

limit.description: Maximum number of views returned (default 50, at most 200).

offset.description: Number of views to skip, from nextOffset of the previous page (default 0).

definitions.name: tables_list_columns
definitions.description: Lists the columns of one table (table_id) or of one view (view_id) the authenticated user can open: id, title, type, subtype, whether a value is mandatory and the options of the type (selection options, number range, text limits, user and group settings). For a view, only the columns the view shows, with whether the view makes each one read-only or mandatory. Give exactly one of table_id and view_id. Read only.

table_id.description: Id of the table, as tables_list_tables returns it. Give this or view_id, not both.

view_id.description: Id of the view, as tables_list_views returns it. Give this or table_id, not both.

definitions.name: tables_list_rows
definitions.description: Lists the rows of one table (table_id) or one view (view_id) the authenticated user can read, as the Tables app reads them: only the columns the view shows (or all columns of the table), and through a view only the rows its saved filter keeps, which you can never widen. Optional filter (groups OR-ed, conditions inside a group AND-ed, on column ids from tables_list_columns or the meta columns -1 id, -2 created by, -3 edited by, -4 created at, -5 edited at), search (text columns and selection labels the user can see), sort and limit; pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page; offsetLimitReached means more rows exist past the deepest page a cursor reaches (narrow the filter). Cells come as {columnId, value} with the native value: a selection gives its option id(s), a relation the id of the related row. Text is cleaned of control characters other than tab and line breaks and of direction marks, and is returned whole up to 20000 characters per cell and 100000 per page; a cut cell carries truncated and totalChars, and truncatedCells counts them. Read only.

table_id.description: Id of the table, as tables_list_tables returns it. Give this or view_id, not both.

view_id.description: Id of the view, as tables_list_views returns it. Give this or table_id, not both.

filter.description: Groups OR-ed together; the conditions inside a group are AND-ed. Always combined with the view's own filter.

column_id.description: Column id from tables_list_columns, or a meta column (-1 id, -2 created by, -3 edited by, -4 created at, -5 edited at).

value.description: The value; a selection option id for a selection column; omit it for is-empty and is-not-empty.

search.description: Text searched in the text columns and the selection labels the user can see.

sort.description: Sort rules in order; without them the view's or table's own sort applies. The row id always breaks ties.

limit.description: Rows per page (default 25, at most 100).

cursor.description: nextCursor of the previous page, with the same other arguments.

definitions.name: tables_create_row
definitions.description: Creates one row in one table (table_id) or one view (view_id) the authenticated user may add rows to, through the Tables app itself, which also fires its events, activity and notifications. cells lists 1 to 100 {column_id, value} pairs, each column once, on the columns tables_list_columns shows for that table or view, never read-only ones; the value follows the column type (see the guide). Without confirm the answer is the plan only; show it, ask, and repeat with confirm: true and its plan_state. A table owned by somebody else also needs confirm_shared: true. Through a view, Tables may fill columns the view does not show so the row matches it.

table_id.description: Id of the table, as tables_list_tables returns it. Give this or view_id, not both.

view_id.description: Id of the view, as tables_list_views returns it. Give this or table_id, not both.

cells.description: The cells to write: a list of 1 to 100 objects {column_id, value}, with nothing else in them and each column_id at most once. value by column type: text a string; link {url, title?} with an http or https url; number a number; stars 0-5 and progress 0-100 as integers; selection an option id; multiple selection a list of option ids; yes/no true or false; date and time "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", "YYYY-MM-DD" or "HH:MM"; users and groups a list of {id, type} with type 0 user, 1 group, 2 team; relation the id of the related row. Numbers, stars and progress also respect the column's minimum and maximum. null empties a cell, except yes/no, stars and progress, which take false or 0, and numbers before Tables 2.3.2, which would store 0.

confirm_shared.description: Set to true, after the user agreed, to write in a table owned by somebody else; the change is seen by everybody the table is shared with.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

definitions.name: tables_update_row
definitions.description: Changes cells of one row (row_id) the authenticated user may read and update, through one table (table_id) or one view (view_id) that shows the row, via the Tables app itself. cells lists 1 to 100 {column_id, value} pairs, each column once, on the columns that table or view shows, never read-only ones; other cells stay as they are. Without confirm the answer is the plan with the values before and after; show it, ask, and repeat with confirm: true and its plan_state. A table owned by somebody else also needs confirm_shared: true.

table_id.description: Id of the table, as tables_list_tables returns it. Give this or view_id, not both.

view_id.description: Id of the view, as tables_list_views returns it. Give this or table_id, not both.

row_id.description: Id of the row, as tables_list_rows returns it.

cells.description: The cells to write: a list of 1 to 100 objects {column_id, value}, with nothing else in them and each column_id at most once. value by column type: text a string; link {url, title?} with an http or https url; number a number; stars 0-5 and progress 0-100 as integers; selection an option id; multiple selection a list of option ids; yes/no true or false; date and time "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", "YYYY-MM-DD" or "HH:MM"; users and groups a list of {id, type} with type 0 user, 1 group, 2 team; relation the id of the related row. Numbers, stars and progress also respect the column's minimum and maximum. null empties a cell, except yes/no, stars and progress, which take false or 0, and numbers before Tables 2.3.2, which would store 0.

confirm_shared.description: Set to true, after the user agreed, to write in a table owned by somebody else; the change is seen by everybody the table is shared with.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

definitions.description: Create one empty Tables table using only the custom template. Plan first; no columns or views are created.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

definitions.name: tables_update_table
definitions.description: Update table title, description, emoji or archived state with native manage permission. Plan first; rows are preserved.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

definitions.name: tables_create_column
definitions.description: Create a typed column in a managed local table. No relation type. A duplicate title may receive a native suffix. Plan first.

options.description: Unique {name,value} entries. Each value is checked against the column type; no raw JSON.

subtype.description: Validated together with type; the empty subtype is explicit.

view_ids.description: Unique managed view IDs in this table to include the new column in.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

definitions.name: tables_update_column
definitions.description: Update column metadata and typed options without changing type or subtype. Preserved fields are written again from a snapshot. No relation edits. Plan first.

options.description: Unique {name,value} entries. Each value is checked against the column type; no raw JSON.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

definitions.name: tables_create_view
definitions.description: Create one empty view in a managed local table. Plan first; rules are edited in a separate call.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

definitions.name: tables_update_view
definitions.description: Update a managed view and its complete columns, filter groups or sort. Rules can hide rows without deleting them. Relation references are preserved only. Plan first.

columns.description: Complete ordered list of unique visible column IDs. Empty clears it. Existing relation references can only be preserved.

filter.description: Complete list of nonempty AND groups, combined with OR. Each rule is {column_id,operator,value}; value is a supported scalar or Tables placeholder. Empty list clears all filters. No relation edits.

sort.description: Complete ordered unique sort rules; empty clears sorting. No relation edits.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

definitions.name: tables_share_node
definitions.description: Share a managed local table or view with an existing user or group and five explicit native permissions. No public links. An identical share is a no-op; different permissions require separate revocation. Plan first.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

definitions.name: tables_unshare_node
definitions.description: Revoke one user/group share of a managed local table or view. Other shares may continue granting access. Plan first.

plan_state.description: Opaque value of the plan. Send it back unchanged together with confirm: true. If the state changed since the plan, nothing is written and the answer is the new plan.

notes: Nextcloud Tables: list the tables and views the user can open, then the columns of one of them, then its rows. A view shows only some rows and columns of its table; for a user who can open only the view, the table and its other columns stay out of reach.

tables_list_rows reads rows of a table or a view; take column ids and selection option ids from tables_list_columns. Filter and sort only on columns the view shows. The placeholders accepted are @me on user and group columns, @checked and @unchecked on yes/no columns, and on date columns @datetime-date-today, @datetime-date-start-of-year, @datetime-date-start-of-month, @datetime-date-start-of-week, @datetime-time-now and @datetime-now, plus @datetime-exact-date:YYYY-MM-DD, @datetime-days-ahead:N and @datetime-days-ago:N from Tables 1.0.10 on: any other value starting with @ is refused. Pages are offsets: rows edited in between can move between pages.

tables_create_row and tables_update_row write one row each, through the Tables app, with a plan first: column ids, option ids and the type of each column come from tables_list_columns. A relation can be written only when the related table or view is readable for the user. Creating through a view is refused when the hidden values that view would fill in cannot be checked. When a confirmed write fails, Tables may or may not have saved it: check before repeating, since repeating a creation can make a second row.

definitions.name: tables_list_tables
definitions.title: List tables
definitions.description: Lists the tables of the Nextcloud Tables app the authenticated user can open: their own, the ones shared with them and the ones of the applications (contexts) they belong to. Each table has an id, its title, whether the user owns it and a link; viewsListed says whether tables_list_views lists its views (only for tables the user owns or manages, as in the Tables app). Read only; it creates nothing. Use limit and offset for more.

limit.description: Maximum number of tables returned (default 50, at most 200).

offset.description: Number of tables to skip, from nextOffset of the previous page (default 0).

definitions.name: tables_list_views
definitions.title: List table views
definitions.description: Lists the views of the Tables app the authenticated user can open: the views of the tables they own or manage, the views shared with them and the views of their applications (contexts). A view shows only some rows and columns of its table. Views of a table shared without manage permission are not listed, as in the Tables app; the table itself is. Read only. Use limit and offset for more.

limit.description: Maximum number of views returned (default 50, at most 200).

offset.description: Number of views to skip, from nextOffset of the previous page (default 0).

definitions.name: tables_list_columns
definitions.title: List table columns
definitions.description: Lists the columns of one table (table_id) or of one view (view_id) the authenticated user can open: id, title, type, subtype, whether a value is mandatory and the options of the type (selection options, number range, text limits, user and group settings). For a view, only the columns the view shows, with whether the view makes each one read-only or mandatory. Give exactly one of table_id and view_id. Read only.

table_id.description: Id of the table, as tables_list_tables returns it. Give this or view_id, not both.

view_id.description: Id of the view, as tables_list_views returns it. Give this or table_id, not both.

definitions.name: tables_list_rows
definitions.title: List table rows
definitions.description: Lists the rows of one table (table_id) or one view (view_id) the authenticated user can read, as the Tables app reads them: only the columns the view shows (or all columns of the table), and through a view only the rows its saved filter keeps, which you can never widen. Optional filter (groups OR-ed, conditions inside a group AND-ed, on column ids from tables_list_columns or the meta columns -1 id, -2 created by, -3 edited by, -4 created at, -5 edited at), search (text columns and selection labels the user can see), sort and limit; pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page; offsetLimitReached means more rows exist past the deepest page a cursor reaches (narrow the filter). Cells come as {columnId, value} with the native value: a selection gives its option id(s), a relation the id of the related row. Text is cleaned of control characters other than tab and line breaks and of direction marks, and is returned whole up to 20000 characters per cell and 100000 per page; a cut cell carries truncated and totalChars, and truncatedCells counts them. Read only.

table_id.description: Id of the table, as tables_list_tables returns it. Give this or view_id, not both.

view_id.description: Id of the view, as tables_list_views returns it. Give this or table_id, not both.

filter.description: Groups OR-ed together; the conditions inside a group are AND-ed. Always combined with the view's own filter.

column_id.description: Column id from tables_list_columns, or a meta column (-1 id, -2 created by, -3 edited by, -4 created at, -5 edited at).

value.description: The value; a selection option id for a selection column; omit it for is-empty and is-not-empty.

search.description: Text searched in the text columns and the selection labels the user can see.

sort.description: Sort rules in order; without them the view's or table's own sort applies. The row id always breaks ties.

limit.description: Rows per page (default 25, at most 100).

cursor.description: nextCursor of the previous page, with the same other arguments.
